title: I built a 2D animation tool, then realized AI could actually rig and animate the characters
author: Crockiestar
selftext:
I originally started this project as a way to quickly animate non-layered character images without redrawing every frame. You could place pins, pose the artwork, and let the software interpolate the movement with smart mesh deformation.

While building it, I realized that AI’s spatial and temporal understanding of rigged characters was getting surprisingly good. It could reason about which pieces were limbs, where joints should pivot, how parts should be connected, and how those relationships should change over time during an animation.

That led me to build **Warp Puppet**, a workspace for assembling layered character pieces into an editable 2D rig. You can use AI to propose the pivots, bones, connections, contacts, and movement behavior, then review everything before accepting it.

The most interesting part for me is how iterative the workflow can be. Instead of treating AI generation as a one-shot result, you can:

* Generate an initial rig
* Test it with different movements
* Ask for specific rig changes in plain language
* Generate an animation such as an idle, walk, attack, or jump
* Refine that animation with additional prompts
* Manually adjust the rig, poses, timing, or individual pin movement at any point

The AI preserves the parts you didn’t ask it to change, so you can gradually improve a rig or animation instead of repeatedly starting over.

The results have honestly been much more impressive than I expected. They’re not always perfect, but having AI operate on an actual editable rig seems far more useful than generating a finished video that’s difficult to change afterward. You still have access to the bones, pins, contacts, keyframes, meshes, and exported game assets.

check it out here [Warp Studio](https://crockiestar.itch.io/warp-studio)

replies.author: Crockiestar
replies.body: I designed the app specifically to make it as easy as possible for the AI to temporally understand the motion and timeline as well as the character rig, which possibly gives better results. You could probably set something like this up in Spine if you build your own, most of the magic is just the AI's ability to understand what you want. But Warp Studio is definetly a competitive powerful tool and much more affordable then some of these companies that charge you insane prices for smart mesh deformation and smart rigging.
